features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or academic credential the letter cites as relevant preparation.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on design or ownership of agent-based systems with explicit constraints, orchestration, or supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as evidenced through concrete engineering problem solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures real experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, or failure handling.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI experience is mentioned vaguely, with no clear production use or reliability detail.
The letter describes shipping AI-backed features or workflows in production.
The letter shows shipped AI work plus concrete attention to trustworthiness, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as serving developers through secure defaults, low friction, and internal-user empathy.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter supports claims with named examples, technical details, mechanisms, or measurements.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central Go appears in the applicant's real working experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but not as a major language in the applicant's work.
Go is presented as a regular or important language for backend work.
Go is clearly described as a primary language or daily driver tied to substantial backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the outcomes or practical effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Learning and collaboration posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and readiness to work closely with security specialists or other internal partners.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures how memorable, cohesive, and well-framed the letter's overall story or voice is.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented skill building through CTFs or similar offensive security practice outside routine product work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution and responsibility in public or upstream codebases, from patches to maintainership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or fixes sent upstream.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintainership, including review or release responsibilities.
The letter shows stewardship of a broadly used project or community, with clear responsibility for releases, roadmap, or contributor management.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and initiative shown through self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and ownership level of relevant professional experience building, launching, operating, or maintaining production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant depth is shown, such as just meeting the baseline or giving little evidence of repeated production ownership.
A solid but moderate track record is shown, such as a few years of experience or several launched services.
A strong track record is shown, with multiple years and repeated production launches or ownership.
An extensive track record is shown, combining multi-year experience with many launched services and clear evidence of sustained production work.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantial and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Reliability and maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, maintainability, testing, failure handling, operability, and long-term ownership in engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role tailoring
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter connects the applicant's background and interest to this exact job's requirements and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through review, analysis, threat modeling, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures understanding of the role as a leverage problem of scaling scarce security expertise through principled automation.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: Captures the strength of formal external certifications or credentials validating security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.name: Security mission fit
features.description: Captures motivation for the role's broader mission of scaling secure-by-default behavior and security impact through foundational tooling.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in software or security with little indication of why this kind of foundational security tooling matters.
Mentions security impact or scale in broad terms but does not develop a strong role-specific point of view.
Clearly frames the role as enabling other engineers or strengthening the development lifecycle across many teams.
Presents a strong, memorable thesis about security as leverage, defaults, quiet resilience, or scaling scarce security judgment.

features.name: Security philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful view of what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or similar security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface professionalism through proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Miscellaneous dimensions that do not clearly belong to any recurring construct above.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
